backtrackingProfile.futureRequirement: A separately versioned request option with independent pattern, record, timeout and output limits and its own compatibility oracle.

benchmark.cachePolicy: Cold compilation resets the bounded compiled-pattern cache before each measured invocation. Warm-cache compiles once before the measured phase; filesystem cache state is not involved.
benchmark.timingBoundary: Safe-profile regex compilation when cold, matching, capture enumeration and deterministic result hashing; fixture construction and JSON serialization are outside the timed boundary.
benchmark.safetyThreshold: Every complete phase median below 1,000 milliseconds; host-bound safety observation, not a cross-engine superiority target.
benchmark.interpretation: The measurements establish safe-profile correctness and bounded host-local execution for the declared workloads. They do not compare against a backtracking engine or claim production superiority.

gateResults.evidence: The focused Search Release suite exited 0 with 166 discovered, 163 passed, 0 failed and 3 expected skips; the exact owning-repository Release suite exited 0 across 21 projects with 1,450 discovered, 1,416 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips.

The separate ownership review approved the safe profile, adversarial handling, cache ownership, compatibility table and benchmark interpretation; exact commands, tool versions, source/artifact hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained.

Focused tests cover pathological safe-profile matching, typed timeout translation, cancellation during dense output and cache eviction/reset ownership release. The benchmark independently checks 20,000 dense capture pairs across seven cold and seven warm trials.

The published compatibility table distinguishes the selected portable non-backtracking profile, the unavailable backtracking profile and literal mode; no request path implicitly enables or falls back to backtracking.

Production limits remain bounded at the pattern, nesting, record, one-second match-timeout and 128-entry compiled-cache levels. Cancellation is observed between emitted matches, timeout is typed, and incomplete runs cannot be reported as successful benchmark measurements.

knownLimitations: The timeout translation unit test uses a sub-millisecond test-only budget for deterministic triggering; production compiled regexes retain the one-second timeout verified by the backend option test and bounded benchmark execution.
The benchmark measures the safe regex backend and capture enumeration in-process. It is not a ripgrep or backtracking baseline and makes no cross-engine superiority claim.
Cancellation is checked between emitted matches; a single match is bounded by the regex timeout rather than asynchronously interrupted inside the .NET engine.
The 128-entry cache releases its strong ownership on eviction/reset; .NET Regex has no IDisposable API, so there is no explicit per-instance disposal call.
The repository-wide suite retains 31 existing expected skips and 3 platform-conditional symlink skips; no package was published, pushed, released or installed.
